questions.q: What is the full-sample Spearman rank correlation between past-5d and forward-5d sector returns, and its Newey-West adjusted t-stat?
options: ≈ +0.45, t ≈ 8.1 — strong momentum
≈ -0.07, t ≈ -2.4 — small but statistically significant reversal
≈ 0.00, t ≈ 0.1 — no relationship at all
≈ -0.90, t ≈ -15 — an almost perfect reversal
questions.explain: The full-sample Spearman rank correlation is approximately -0.07, with a Newey-West (HAC) adjusted t-stat of approximately -2.4 — small but statistically significant evidence of reversal.

questions.q: Why are Newey-West (HAC) standard errors needed for this test instead of a plain OLS t-test?
options: Because the data contains missing values
Because overlapping 5-day return windows induce autocorrelation that a plain t-test formula doesn't account for, which would otherwise overstate statistical confidence
Because Spearman correlation cannot be tested for significance any other way
Because the sample includes more than one ETF
questions.explain: Overlapping 5-day windows share days with each other, inducing autocorrelation. HAC/Newey-West standard errors correct for this so the t-stat isn't artificially inflated.

questions.q: What does the ADF test on the winner-minus-loser spread show, and why does it matter?
options: It fails to reject the unit root, suggesting the spread trends indefinitely
It rejects the unit root at the 5% level (p ≈ 0.02), confirming the spread is mean-reverting rather than trending
It shows the spread is identical to a white-noise series with zero mean reversion
It cannot be computed because the spread is not stationary by definition
questions.explain: The ADF test rejects the unit-root null at the 5% level (p ≈ 0.02), meaning the winner-minus-loser spread behaves like a mean-reverting series, not a random walk.

questions.q: What does the VIX-tercile split reveal about the reversal effect?
options: The effect is identical regardless of VIX regime
The effect is significant in the high-VIX tercile (IC ≈ -0.11, t ≈ -2.9) but not significant in the low-VIX tercile (IC ≈ -0.02, t ≈ -0.6)
The effect only exists in the low-VIX tercile
The VIX has no measurable relationship to the reversal effect
questions.explain: The reversal effect concentrates in high-VIX regimes (significant) and is statistically indistinguishable from zero in low-VIX regimes, confirming regime dependence.

questions.q: What is 'data snooping,' and why is it flagged as a risk in this lesson?
options: Illegally accessing a competitor's proprietary trading data
The risk that testing many related cuts of the same dataset increases the chance that at least one result looks significant purely by luck
A technique for cleaning missing values in a dataset
A method for improving the accuracy of the ADF test
questions.explain: Data snooping is the risk that running multiple related tests on the same data (full-sample, ADF, three VIX terciles) raises the odds of a spuriously 'significant' result, even with a sound hypothesis.
